Problem: The people of Evenland never use odd digits. Instead of counting 1,2,3,4,5,6, an Evenlander counts 2, 4, 6, 8, 20, 22. This system is essentially a base-5 numeral system but with all the digits doubled. Convert the integer 111 from base-10 to the Evenlanders' version. Provide your answer as a single number.

<reflection>
I have not yet established any correct intermediate conclusions.
Evenland also uses the digit 0, as shown by 20. The doubled base-5 digits are {0, 2, 4, 6, 8}, so excluding 0 is incorrect.
Use the full digit set {0, 2, 4, 6, 8}; convert 111 to base 5 first, then double each base-5 digit.
</reflection>
